title: UN Women Entrepreneurship Expo 2026/2027: Business Bootcamps, Mentorship, Investment Pitching and Networking for Women Entrepreneurs in Europe and Central Asia
summary: The UN Women Entrepreneurship Expo 2026/2027 is bringing together women entrepreneurs and business partners from Europe and Central Asia for a regional platform focused on entrepreneurship development, business networking, capacity building, mentorship and investment readiness. The Expo is designed around the principles of inclusivity, diversity and leaving no one behind . It will combine local and interregional business-building activities, networking opportunities and capacity-building workshops, giving women entrepreneurs the opportunity to strengthen their businesses, connect with peers and business partners, receive expert support and prepare for potential investment opportunities. The programme will culminate in Expo Capital Quest , a physical event planned for Spring 2027 , where selected participants will have the opportunity to take part in networking and investor pitching, subject to an additional selection process. What Is the UN Women Entrepreneurship Expo 2026/2027? The UN Women Entrepreneurship Expo 2026/2027 is a regional entrepreneurship initiative designed to support women entrepreneurs and women-owned businesses in Europe and Central Asia. Rather than being a single conference or exhibition, the Expo consists of several interconnected activities intended to help participating entrepreneurs develop their businesses and expand their networks. The programme includes: Local business-building activities. Interregional networking activities. Capacity-building workshops. Business bootcamps. Mentorship. Investment-pitch preparation. Feedback from experts. Online business exhibition opportunities. Networking with entrepreneurs from across the region. Potential participation in a physical investor-focused event. The programme is therefore particularly relevant to women entrepreneurs who are already developing a product or service and want to improve their business capabilities, visibility, networks and readiness for future growth or investment. Key Highlights of the UN Women Entrepreneurship Expo The Expo provides women entrepreneurs with access to several forms of business development support. Main opportunities include: Online business exhibition: Participants can showcase their businesses through an online exhibition space. Business bootcamps: Selected entrepreneurs will have the opportunity to participate in bootcamps managed by leading companies. Mentorship: Participants can receive support and guidance from mentors. Investment preparation: Entrepreneurs can prepare their investment pitches and receive feedback. Regional networking: Participants can connect with entrepreneurs and peers from countries across Europe and Central Asia. Expo Capital Quest: Selected participants may take part in a physical event in Spring 2027 focused on networking and investor pitching. Who Is the UN Women Entrepreneurship Expo For? The Expo is primarily intended for women entrepreneurs and representatives of women-owned businesses . The programme is open to women entrepreneurs working across all sectors of the economy . Applicants are expected to provide information about themselves and their businesses, including their business ownership, location, business development stage, sector, online presence, revenue, financing history, business challenges, training needs and future growth plans. This means the application process is designed not simply to collect basic registration information but also to help the Expo organisers understand each entrepreneur s business needs and tailor the programme s content accordingly. Business Stage Requirements One of the most important aspects of the Expo is the stage of business development. The programme states that, to be eligible for all phases of the Expo , a woman entrepreneur or representative of a women-owned business should be at one of the following stages: Minimum Viable Product (MVP) Early Stage , where the business is already selling Growth Stage , where the business is generating revenue These stages indicate that the Expo is particularly focused on entrepreneurs who have moved beyond the purely conceptual stage and have something tangible to develop, sell or scale. However, the application questionnaire also allows applicants to identify themselves as being at: Idea Stage Working on Prototype Minimum Viable Product (MVP) Early Stage Growth Stage Not applicable The form explains that entrepreneurs who meet the applicable criteria can participate in the virtual Expo capacity-development and networking component , while virtual booths will be allocated to entrepreneurs who already have an MVP, are already selling, or are at the Growth Stage. This distinction is important for applicants because being at an earlier stage may affect the specific elements of the Expo in which they can participate. Countries Eligible for the UN Women Entrepreneurship Expo The Expo focuses on Europe and Central Asia . The application form specifically lists the following countries: Albania Armenia Azerbaijan Bosnia and Herzegovina Georgia Kazakhstan Kosovo (under UNSCR 1244) Kyrgyzstan Moldova Montenegro North Macedonia Serbia Tajikistan Türkiye Ukraine The questionnaire also includes an “Other” option for the country where the applicant s company is registered or operating. The programme description refers to networking with peers from 12 countries of Europe and Central Asia , while the application questionnaire itself lists 15 named countries plus an “Other” option. Applicants should therefore carefully provide their actual country and business location when completing the form. Learn More HERE. Business Sectors Eligible for the Expo Women entrepreneurs from all sectors of the economy can apply for participation in the Expo. The application form provides a broad list of sectors, including: Agriculture Building and construction Media and communication ICT and telecommunications Training and education Clothing, fashion and textiles Trade, transport and logistics Healthcare Tourism and hospitality Finance Water, sanitation and waste management Energy Food products Retail Sports Jewellery and accessories Environment Paper products Electronics Other sectors This broad sectoral approach means that the Expo is not restricted to technology startups or a single industry. Women building businesses in traditional industries as well as innovative, technology-driven and sustainability-focused sectors can potentially benefit. UN Women also states that it reserves the right to exclude certain products from the Expo following careful consideration. Benefits of Participating in the UN Women Entrepreneurship Expo 1. Showcase Your Business Online Participants can showcase their businesses through an online exhibition space . This provides entrepreneurs with an opportunity to increase the visibility of their products or services and present their businesses to a wider network of potential partners and other stakeholders. For entrepreneurs looking to strengthen their digital presence, the online exhibition component can be an important opportunity to communicate their value proposition and business story. 2. Participate in Business Bootcamps Selected women entrepreneurs will be invited to participate in business bootcamps managed by leading companies . These bootcamps are intended to support business development and help entrepreneurs strengthen practical capabilities relevant to running and growing a business. Participation in bootcamps will vary by country, and selected participants will receive additional information from the organisers. 3. Receive Mentorship The Expo provides opportunities for entrepreneurs to receive support from mentors . Mentorship can be particularly valuable for entrepreneurs dealing with challenges such as business strategy, market access, financing, marketing, technology adoption, operations and growth. The questionnaire also asks applicants about their current levels of knowledge in areas such as financial management, marketing, networking, branding, distribution, international markets and competitiveness. This information is intended to help the organisers better understand participants needs. 4. Prepare an Investment Pitch Another major benefit is the opportunity to prepare an investment pitch and receive feedback . Investment readiness is especially relevant for entrepreneurs who want to attract capital to expand their businesses. Applicants are asked about their business objectives, including whether they want to find investment to move to the next phase of development and whether they want to become more attractive to investors. The Expo therefore provides a platform for entrepreneurs to improve how they communicate their business opportunity to potential investors. 5. Build Regional Business Networks Participants will have opportunities to network with other entrepreneurs and business partners from the Europe and Central Asia region. Networking can help entrepreneurs identify: Potential business partners. New buyers. Suppliers. Investors. Mentors. Industry experts. Other entrepreneurs. Regional and international opportunities. For businesses seeking to expand beyond their existing market, regional networking can be particularly valuable. Learn More HERE. Expo Capital Quest 2027 One of the major planned components of the programme is the Expo Capital Quest , a physical event expected to take place in Spring 2027 . The event will provide opportunities for networking and investor pitching. However, participation in Expo Capital Quest is subject to an additional selection process . Therefore, completing the initial Expo application does not automatically guarantee participation in the physical Capital Quest event. Entrepreneurs interested in investment should therefore treat the initial application as an opportunity to demonstrate the strength and potential of their business while recognising that additional selection may apply for the Capital Quest component. Regional Virtual Expo 2026 The Regional Virtual Expo 2026 is scheduled to take place in November 2026 . According to the programme information, this virtual component will be open to all women entrepreneurs interested . The virtual Expo forms part of the broader regional programme and provides an opportunity for entrepreneurs to engage in online capacity development and networking. Selected entrepreneurs may subsequently be invited to participate in country-specific bootcamps and satellite events. Country-Specific Bootcamps and Satellite Events The Expo is not limited to one uniform programme for every participant. Selected women entrepreneurs will be invited to participate in Bootcamp and Satellite Events , with activities varying from country to country. Participants who are selected for these activities will receive additional information regarding the specific opportunities available to them. This structure allows the programme to respond to different business environments, sectors and needs across the participating countries. What Information Do Applicants Need to Provide? The application questionnaire is comprehensive and asks applicants to provide detailed information about themselves and their businesses. Applicants should be prepared to provide information covering several areas. Personal and Contact Information The form requests: First name Surname Contact phone number Country and city, town or village Email address Gender Age category Geographic location Applicants are asked to provide a full telephone number with the country code, and the programme indicates that having a number available on WhatsApp is preferable. Business Ownership and Location Applicants will be asked whether they: Own or co-own the registered business. Have participated in a previous Expo. Operate or have a company registered in a particular country. The form asks applicants to identify the country where their company is registered or operating. Online Business Presence Applicants are also asked whether they currently sell products or services online. The available responses distinguish between: Businesses that operate entirely online. Businesses that sell some products or services online. Businesses that do not currently sell products or services online. This information helps the organisers understand participants current level of digital business activity. Business Description Applicants must provide a description of their company in fewer than 150 words . The description should explain: What the business offers. Who the customers are. What traction the business has achieved. What the entrepreneur wants to accomplish through the business. Links to any existing articles about the company, where applicable. Entrepreneurs should therefore prepare a concise but compelling description before starting the application. Business Size Applicants will also be asked to indicate the size of their business: Solo entrepreneur or micro business: 1–10 employees Small business: 11–50 employees Medium business: 51–250 employees This enables the organisers to understand the scale of participating enterprises. Annual Business Revenue Applicants are asked to identify their approximate average annual revenue in US dollars. The available categories are: Less than US$50,000 US$50,000–100,000 US$100,000–500,000 More than US$500,000 This information can help the programme assess the different stages and financial profiles of participating businesses. Business Challenges Applicants are asked to identify up to three of the biggest challenges they experienced when starting their businesses. Potential challenges include: Accessing financing Getting support from family Finding a suitable business location Finding information about starting a business Registration and regulatory requirements Knowing where to obtain business advice Finding suppliers Getting customers Family and childcare responsibilities Other challenges This section is particularly relevant because it allows the Expo organisers to identify common barriers facing women entrepreneurs and tailor support accordingly. Business Financing The application asks entrepreneurs about the sources of financing they used when starting their businesses. Possible sources include: Personal savings Sale of an asset Bank loans Private investors Government programmes Family and friends Microfinance institutions International donor-funded projects Other sources Applicants are also asked whether they have attempted to obtain a business loan within the previous year. Barriers to Accessing Business Loans Entrepreneurs who have experience seeking financing can identify the challenges they face when trying to obtain a loan from a bank or microfinance institution. Possible barriers include: High collateral requirements High interest rates Loan amounts being too small Short repayment periods Personal guarantee requirements Co-signer requirements Difficulty preparing business plans and financial statements Perceived lack of seriousness toward women entrepreneurs by loan officers Other barriers This section provides the Expo with insight into the financing constraints affecting participating women-owned businesses. Business Networks and Associations Applicants are asked whether they belong to business-related organisations, such as: Chambers of commerce or industry Business associations Women s business or women entrepreneurs associations Industry-specific associations Employers associations Other business organisations Participation in such organisations can contribute to networking, market access and knowledge sharing. Sources of Business Information The application also asks entrepreneurs where they normally obtain most of their business-related information. Possible sources include: Newspapers Government publications Chambers of commerce Business associations Lawyers Accountants Business development or enterprise centres Professional business advisers Other male business owners Other female business owners Mentors Family, friends and neighbours Internet Television Radio Applicants are asked to identify no more than three of their most important sources. Previous Trade Fair and Exhibition Experience Applicants will be asked whether they have participated in: Local trade fairs National trade fairs Regional trade fairs International trade fairs No trade fairs or exhibitions This information helps the organisers understand applicants previous experience with showcasing their businesses and interacting with potential customers and partners. Previous Training and Business Support The questionnaire asks whether applicants have received business or skills training through organisations or companies. They can indicate whether they have received: Training from UN Women Training from other organisations No business or skills training Applicants are also asked whether they have previously participated in programmes specifically supporting women entrepreneurs. These may include: Loan programmes for women entrepreneurs Entrepreneurship or self-employment training Women s business support or enterprise centres Government procurement programmes targeting women-owned businesses Women s trade fairs or exhibitions Business counselling or mentoring Other women-focused business support programmes Digital and ICT Skills The application assesses applicants understanding of how technology can support their businesses. Applicants are asked to assess their awareness of how they can use: Smartphones for business Computers for business The Internet for business This information can help the programme understand participants existing digital capabilities and potential training needs. Business Growth Plans for the Next 12 Months Applicants are asked how they intend to develop or improve their businesses over the following 12 months. Potential plans include: Investing in new equipment or technology Increasing the number of employees Reducing the number of employees Expanding products or services Reducing products or services Developing a website to increase online sales Joining an e-commerce platform Moving to larger premises Integrating information technology into business operations and marketing Adopting more environmentally responsible practices Other growth plans These questions encourage applicants to think strategically about where they want their businesses to be in the near future. International Expansion Entrepreneurs are also asked whether they intend to expand or establish their businesses in other locations . This is particularly relevant to women entrepreneurs seeking regional or international market expansion. The Expo s networking and business-building components may be useful for entrepreneurs interested in establishing partnerships beyond their current markets. Business Targets Applicants are asked to identify the targets they have defined for their businesses during the year. These may include: Increasing the number of customers Increasing revenue Finding investment to move to the next phase Improving the business model Diversifying the business model Revising the business model Building partnerships nationally, regionally or globally Conducting due diligence Working with sector experts Increasing technical capabilities Becoming more attractive to investors Other targets This section provides applicants with an opportunity to demonstrate their ambitions and priorities. Areas Where Applicants May Need Training The application asks entrepreneurs to identify up to three areas in which they would like training for themselves or their staff. Potential areas include: General management and strategic planning Understanding markets Inventory management Sources of finance and access to loans Financial management ICT adoption Efficiency and productivity Product development Supplier relationships Buyer relationships E-commerce marketing and sales Crisis management Applicants can therefore use the questionnaire to communicate the specific skills and knowledge gaps they want the Expo to help address. Technical Assistance Available Through the Programme In addition to training, applicants are asked whether they could benefit from technical assistance during the next two years. Possible areas include: Establishing market links with new buyers Establishing market links with new suppliers Access to finance Productivity improvements Other technical assistance This reinforces the Expo s broader objective of providing practical business development support rather than simply creating a networking event. Innovative, Technology and Green Businesses The questionnaire asks entrepreneurs whether their businesses are: Technology startups Related to innovative products or services Related to green or sustainable products or services Women entrepreneurs working in these areas can therefore identify the innovative or sustainability-related nature of their businesses as part of the application. Information Sharing and Data Protection The application includes an information-sharing consent section. Applicants are informed that personal identifying information will be kept confidential and used exclusively for the purposes of the Women’s Entrepreneurship Expo . The information will be stored according to UN Women data protection standards . Applicants can indicate whether they agree to their information being shared with Expo organisers and partners in accordance with the stated data protection standards. The form also explains that consent is voluntary and can be withdrawn. Applicants who have questions or wish to withdraw their consent are directed to contact contact.expo@unwomen.org . Applicants can additionally indicate whether they would like to receive future updates from UN Women. Application Deadline A specific application deadline is not provided in the information supplied for the UN Women Entrepreneurship Expo 2026/2027. Applicants should therefore avoid assuming that the November 2026 Regional Virtual Expo date is the application deadline. The information provided states that: The Regional Virtual Expo 2026 will take place in November 2026 . The Expo Capital Quest is planned for Spring 2027 , subject to additional selection. Selected women entrepreneurs will receive further information about Bootcamps and Satellite Events. Because no specific closing date is included in the supplied application information, applicants should check the official Expo application platform and UN Women announcements for the current application deadline before submitting. Click HERE to Apply! How to Prepare a Strong Application Women entrepreneurs interested in participating should prepare their information before completing the questionnaire. A strong application should clearly communicate: What your business does — Explain your product or service clearly. Who your customers are — Identify your target market. Your traction — Highlight sales, revenue, customers, partnerships or other evidence of progress. Your business stage — Clearly indicate whether you are at MVP, Early Stage or Growth Stage. Your growth objectives — Explain what you want to achieve over the next 12 months. Your financing needs — Be clear about whether you are seeking investment or other forms of financial support. Your training needs — Select areas where the programme could provide meaningful value. Your expansion plans — Explain whether you intend to enter new markets or locations. Your investment ambitions — If relevant, explain how investment would help your business move to its next phase. Your online presence — Provide relevant websites, social media pages or articles about your business where appropriate. Why Women Entrepreneurs Should Consider the Expo The UN Women Entrepreneurship Expo 2026/2027 offers a combination of business visibility, entrepreneurship training, mentorship, networking and investment preparation . For women entrepreneurs who have already developed an MVP, started selling or reached the revenue-generating stage, the programme could provide an opportunity to move their businesses toward greater visibility and growth. It may be particularly useful for entrepreneurs who want to: Strengthen their business model. Improve financial management. Develop stronger branding. Expand their customer base. Find new buyers. Develop supplier relationships. Access finance. Prepare for investors. Improve their digital presence. Enter international markets. Connect with other women entrepreneurs. Receive mentorship. Build regional partnerships. Develop more sustainable business practices. The questionnaire itself demonstrates the broad range of business-development needs the programme is designed to understand and potentially address. Pro Tip for Applicants Do not treat the application as merely a registration form. Use it as an opportunity to clearly present the strength, traction, challenges and future potential of your business. Before applying, prepare a concise business description of fewer than 150 words, gather information about your revenue and business size, identify your biggest business challenges and training needs, and clearly define what you want to accomplish over the next 12 months. If you are already at the MVP, Early or Growth Stage, clearly demonstrate your progress and explain how participation in the Expo could help you scale, access markets, build partnerships or become more investment-ready. Conclusion The UN Women Entrepreneurship Expo 2026/2027 provides a comprehensive platform for women entrepreneurs and women-owned businesses in Europe and Central Asia to strengthen their enterprises, build networks and prepare for future growth. The programme goes beyond a conventional business exhibition by combining online showcasing, capacity-building workshops, business bootcamps, mentorship, investment-pitch preparation, expert feedback and regional networking . Women entrepreneurs can use the opportunity to identify their business challenges, improve their skills, develop connections with potential buyers and partners, explore financing opportunities and prepare their businesses for expansion. The planned Regional Virtual Expo in November 2026 will provide a major online networking and capacity-building opportunity, while selected entrepreneurs may subsequently participate in country-specific Bootcamps and Satellite Events. A further selection process may also lead to participation in Expo Capital Quest , a physical networking and investor-pitching event planned for Spring 2027 . Because the supplied application information does not state a specific application deadline, prospective applicants should monitor the official UN Women Entrepreneurship Expo channels and application platform for the latest submission instructions and closing date. Overall, the Expo is particularly relevant to women entrepreneurs who already have a tangible business, product or service and want to strengthen their capabilities, increase visibility, connect with regional peers and business partners, and position their businesses for future investment and expansion. title: Global EbA Fund Grants 2026: Up to $500,000 for Ecosystem-Based Adaptation Projects in Developing Countries
summary: The Global EbA Fund Grants 2026 provide an important funding opportunity for organisations working to address climate change, strengthen ecosystem resilience and advance Ecosystem-based Adaptation (EbA) in vulnerable countries. For the 2026 funding cycle, the Global EbA Fund is inviting organisations to submit innovative and catalytic proposals designed to overcome systemic barriers that prevent Ecosystem-based Adaptation from being adopted, scaled and mainstreamed. The calls place particular emphasis on Small Island Developing States (SIDS) and Least Developed Countries (LDCs) , where climate vulnerability is often high while institutional, technical and financial capacity remains constrained. The 2026 calls provide two grant tracks: Small-Size Grants of up to US$250,000 and Medium-Size Grants of up to US$500,000 . Both tracks support projects of up to 24 months and seek initiatives capable of creating lasting enabling conditions for climate adaptation rather than simply financing isolated conservation activities. What Is the Global EbA Fund? The Global EbA Fund is a funding mechanism focused on creating an enabling environment for the implementation and scaling of Ecosystem-based Adaptation . Ecosystem-based Adaptation uses the conservation, restoration and sustainable management of ecosystems to help people and communities adapt to the impacts of climate change. Rather than treating climate adaptation solely as an infrastructure or technological challenge, EbA recognises the important role that healthy ecosystems can play in reducing climate vulnerability. The Fund supports innovative initiatives that address the systemic obstacles preventing EbA from being effectively adopted and expanded. These obstacles can include gaps in: Climate and environmental data Scientific evidence Technical capacity Institutional capacity Governance Policy implementation Financing Investment readiness Knowledge sharing Awareness Partnerships and collaboration According to the information provided, the Fund has been operational since 2020 and, as of June 2026, had supported 75 projects across 41 countries , with 29 projects completed and 46 at various stages of implementation . Its portfolio covers a wide range of ecosystems and landscapes, including: Coastal and marine environments Drylands Grasslands Forests Mountains Urban areas River basins Wetlands This broad portfolio demonstrates that Ecosystem-based Adaptation can be applied across different ecological, social and economic contexts. The Fund s overall objective is to finance innovative approaches capable of overcoming systemic barriers and enabling EbA to be taken up, scaled and mainstreamed. Learn More HERE Why the 2026 Global EbA Fund Call Matters Climate change is increasing pressure on communities, economies and ecosystems around the world. Rising temperatures, droughts, floods, storms, changing rainfall patterns, sea-level rise and other climate-related hazards are affecting food security, water security, livelihoods and socioeconomic development. At the same time, many ecosystems are being degraded through unsustainable resource use and other pressures. This creates a double challenge: communities become increasingly exposed to climate risks while the ecosystems that could help protect them become less capable of providing essential services. Ecosystem-based Adaptation seeks to address these interconnected challenges by strengthening the health and resilience of ecosystems while also reducing vulnerability among people. The 2026 Global EbA Fund calls are particularly relevant to Small Island Developing States and Least Developed Countries . SIDS are highly vulnerable to climate impacts because of factors such as their small land areas, remoteness and close connections between communities, oceans and ecosystems. They can face increasingly frequent and intense tropical cyclones, storm surges, heatwaves, droughts, flooding, changing precipitation patterns and sea-level rise. LDCs also face significant climate vulnerability. Their economies frequently depend heavily on climate-sensitive sectors, while limited institutional and financial capacity can make it difficult to recover from climate-related shocks or mobilise sufficient resources for adaptation. The call therefore seeks projects that do more than implement individual adaptation activities. It seeks initiatives capable of strengthening the systems, institutions, knowledge, partnerships and investment mechanisms needed to enable EbA to grow over the long term. Global EbA Fund Small-Size Grants 2026 The Small-Size Grants Call for Proposals is intended to support innovative and catalytic initiatives that address systemic barriers to scaling Ecosystem-based Adaptation. Small-Size Grant Amount The Fund will provide grants of up to US$250,000 per project . The provided call information indicates that the Small-Size Grants track will support 10 grants , with projects lasting between 18 and 24 months . The official webpage specifies a maximum project duration of 24 months. Small-Size Grants Deadline Applications for the Small-Size Grants can be submitted through the online platform from: 28 September to 26 October 2026 The application deadline is 26 October 2026 . The call was officially launched on 24 August 2026 . Click HERE to download the Small-size Call for Proposals Document. What the Small-Size Grants Will Support The Small-Size Grants call is looking for projects that address upstream or systemic barriers preventing the uptake and scaling of Ecosystem-based Adaptation. Successful proposals should contribute to one or more areas such as: 1. Strengthening Institutional and Technical Capacity Projects can address institutional or technical limitations that prevent organisations, governments and other stakeholders from effectively implementing EbA. This could include initiatives that improve technical expertise, institutional systems, planning capacity or decision-making processes. 2. Improving Data and Evidence Strong evidence is essential for convincing policymakers, investors and other stakeholders to support adaptation approaches. The Fund therefore welcomes projects that generate, improve or apply quality data and evidence to resolve specific barriers to EbA implementation and investment. 3. Building Knowledge and Learning Networks Projects can strengthen systematic knowledge exchange, learning networks and communities of practice that enable practitioners and decision-makers to learn from successful EbA approaches. 4. Improving Investment Readiness The call encourages initiatives that prepare projects and concepts capable of attracting larger-scale climate financing. This can include developing investable project pipelines, strengthening financial models and preparing scalable concepts that can eventually move beyond small grant funding. 5. Supporting Innovative EbA Technologies Projects may adapt or scale tested technological solutions for particular socio-ecological systems. The emphasis is on technologies that can generate useful lessons for practitioners and decision-makers and contribute to broader EbA uptake. 6. Conducting Applied and Functional Research The Fund is interested in practical research that addresses specific obstacles to EbA implementation or investment. Research should therefore have a clear application and contribute to solving real-world adaptation challenges. 7. Creating Synergies With Other Initiatives Applicants are encouraged to work with existing Ecosystem-based Adaptation and Nature-based Solution initiatives where this can generate operational synergies, strengthen collaboration and create opportunities for co-financing. These areas are explicitly highlighted in the Small-Size Grants call. What Makes a Strong Global EbA Fund Proposal? The Fund s evaluation criteria provide applicants with a useful indication of what reviewers will be looking for. Ecosystem-Based Adaptation — 30% The proposal must clearly demonstrate that it is an EbA intervention and explain how it will reduce vulnerability or increase the resilience of human communities to climate change. Applicants should clearly identify: The main climate hazards. The climate risks involved. The affected communities. Ecosystem vulnerabilities. The ecosystem services involved. How the proposed intervention will reduce vulnerability. The proposal should establish a convincing connection between ecosystem management and climate adaptation outcomes. Innovative and Catalytic Contribution — 30% Innovation and catalytic potential are also worth 30% of the evaluation. The Fund wants interventions capable of producing systemic change. Examples could include initiatives that: Influence policy. Address institutional capacity gaps. Develop new financing mechanisms. Improve governance. Strengthen investment readiness. Demonstrate approaches that can be replicated elsewhere. Test approaches in new contexts. The key question is not simply whether the project is innovative, but whether it can help trigger broader transformation in how EbA is implemented or financed. Sustainability — 20% Sustainability accounts for 20% of the evaluation. Applicants need to explain how activities and results will continue beyond the grant period, including opportunities for replication and upscaling. Proposals should also demonstrate connections to relevant national and international policies and synergies with other initiatives. Institutional Arrangements — 20% Institutional arrangements account for another 20% . The applicant organisation should have: An appropriate organisational structure. Adequate financial capacity. Strong internal controls. Qualified and dedicated staff. Relevant technical expertise. Previous experience implementing projects of similar scope and complexity. This means applicants should not focus exclusively on the technical idea. They must also demonstrate that their organisation has the capacity to responsibly manage the proposed funding and deliver the project. Theory of Change, Logical Framework and SMART Indicators A strong application should have a clear and logical Theory of Change . The Fund expects the results chain to demonstrate how proposed activities will lead to outputs and outcomes that create an enabling environment for reducing identified climate risks. The project design should include: A logical and coherent results chain. Feasible activities. A realistic implementation timeline. SMART indicators. Appropriate data sources. Defined reporting intervals. A budget that corresponds logically with activities and timelines. Applicants must also use the Global EbA Fund s Core Indicator Framework . At least three relevant indicators from the Core Indicator Framework must be incorporated into the project s logical framework. Existing Work Is Important A key eligibility requirement is that the proposed project must be built on or based on existing work . Applicants should therefore avoid presenting an entirely disconnected idea with no evidence of previous activity, experience or groundwork. A stronger proposal can demonstrate: Previous pilot activities. Existing partnerships. Prior research. Community engagement. Existing institutional relationships. Previous data or evidence. Lessons learned. Existing projects that can be scaled or replicated. This helps demonstrate that the proposed investment can move an existing concept toward greater impact rather than starting from zero.
